messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE triggered — streaming.p99 spike detected on /v1/stream (eu-west-1) · paging oncall-frontend · runbook: https://go/runbooks/streaming-tail
oncall-frontend: reading dashboard now. p95 ~ 210ms, p99 spiking to ~12s on SSE & websocket routes. Error rate low but a lot of stalled chunks/clients disconnecting. Seeing increases starting 2026-03-15T12:34:02Z.
aj: ack, I'm on it. any customer-reported errors yet?
customer-success: got 3 inbound tickets — two enterprise customers reporting intermittent stalls and reconnects. flagged urgent to AE.
maria: looking at edge-proxy logs for eu-west-1. seeing write-backpressure warnings from stream-proxy pods. sample:
```
[2026-03-15T12:35:01Z] stream-proxy[pid=2356] WARN write_buffer_full backlog=18432 client=10.4.7.12 route=/v1/stream upstream=svc-runtime:8080
[2026-03-15T12:35:02Z] stream-proxy ERROR upstream_timeout id=abc123 duration=30.2s
```
maria: also seeing KV cache evictions on a few runtime nodes at the same timeframe — cache churn could be causing longer tail for cold KV lookups.
devon: interesting — are we seeing client slow consumers (backpressure) or server-side stalls? trace shows a bunch of long pause events inside runtime while serializing chunks.
eli: I grabbed a tail of the worker metrics — event_loop_latency p99 bumped to 350ms and there are spike clusters in the chunking queue length.
aj: hypothesis: mix of client backpressure + proxy buffer saturation + occasional long serialization from runtime (cold cache). mitigation options: (A) increase proxy_write_timeout and buffer to avoid premature disconnects (B) force short-term route fallback to smaller-chunk model variant (C) evict heavy consumers by tightening slow-consumer policy.
oncall-frontend: which is fastest to try? we need something reversible with low risk.
devon: fastest = increase proxy write timeout and reduce buffer_coalesce window to force more frequent flushes. apply to edge-proxy as a canary in eu-west-1.
maria: I can roll the proxy patch. command I'll run (canary):
```
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/edge-proxy PROXY_WRITE_TIMEOUT=60 PROXY_COALESCE_MS=50 --record
```
maria: starting canary now on 2/6 edge-proxy pods in eu-west-1. will watch.

(12:36:40) maria: canary deployed
eli: metrics: p99 for stream route dropped from 12.1s -> 3.4s in the canary subset. connection drops down ~70% for those pods.
aj: good signal. roll to rest of pods with 1 minute stagger.
maria: rolling remaining pods now.

(12:39:05) devon: another quick tweak — enable immediate_chunk_flush header for internal clients as a fallback. added a header transform rule in API gateway for customers on affected plans.

(12:40:12) customer-success: notified affected customers with temporary mitigation steps (reconnect recommended, backoff 1s -> 2s). ticket updates sent.

(12:41:30) eli: after full roll p99 is down to ~1.9s, p95 200ms. error disconnects are now at baseline. still seeing a few latency tail events on specific runtime nodes.
aj: great. next steps: 1) leave proxy timeouts higher for 2 hours 2) gather runtime traces for cold-serialization paths 3) postmortem to identify KV eviction pattern and chunking hotpath.
oncall-frontend: I'll keep monitoring for 30m and page if it reoccurs.

devon: assigning postmortem owners: devon (runtime chunking), maria (proxy config & rollout), eli (metrics & alerts). I'll create a postmortem doc and link.

(12:44:01) incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — status: mitigated, impact: partial (stream stalls reported, resolved by proxy config roll), severity: sev2 -> followup required. pinging #oncall-rotations for blameless postmortem.

customer-success: customers acknowledged the workaround and appreciate fast response. will hold on tickets until root-cause fix.
aj: closing this handoff thread — if anyone sees recurrence reopen. :white_check_mark:

maria: note: we left PROXY_WRITE_TIMEOUT=60 and PROXY_COALESCE_MS=50 in prod as temporary config. will revert after RCA or replace with more targeted fix.
devon: logging the internal trace IDs for the worst offenders: abc123, def456, ghi789 — saved to S3 at s3://redwood-ops/incident-1789456789/traces

oncall-frontend: thanks team — handing back to SRE rotation. :heavy_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED for now — followup: postmortem id=pm-1789456789 assigned to devon+maria+eli.
